label: D2 a2->S2 common after an unrewarded a2 trial, growing late in episode, larger when S2 believed good
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 50, 0, 50) * (1 - belief) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 50, 0, 50) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (ep_trial >= 80) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (ep_trial >= 70)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.7% of steps), active only at D2. It fires when the agent has just chosen a2 and reached S2 via the common transition, and the previous trial was also a2 and went unrewarded (a2 S1 u or a2 S2 u). The magnitude rises with trial in the episode (about zero before trial 50, largest around trials 80-90, a little lower at 90+). It is larger when the ideal observer believes S2 is good (low belief), a bit larger when the previous a2 trial was a rare S1 transition, and small after a rewarded a2 trial late in the episode. It is ~0 at D1 and GO and after any a1 trial. The interaction (this choice/state x last trial x episode time) is the key: on dev, the base conjunction times an episode ramp gives R^2 0.48 beyond timing, the belief and late-episode refinements raise it to 0.52, and test is 0.525. That is well above the additive all ceiling (0.19) and the all-observed ceiling (0.16), because the cues are multiplicative. Uses only observed variables (this trial action/state are known at D2), so nothing is lost against the earlier model-value explanation as far as this score shows. The largest misses are single ~1.9 spikes that the model under-predicts at about 0.5-0.6.

issues: The core claims hold up. The recorded test R^2 beyond timing of 0.525 reproduces exactly. Every other D2 cell, fitted separately for ep_dec>=6, sits near -0.04, which just cancels the timing baseline: a2->S2 after rewarded a2, a2->S1 rare after unrewarded a2, any a1 choice after unrewarded a2, and a2->S2 after a1. The conjunction cell itself is +0.28. D1 and GO residuals are 0. So 'only D2, only a2->S2 common after unrewarded a2' is correct.

The episode ramp checks out (per-decile weights on the conjunction, test): <=d3 0.005, d4 0.012, d5 0.033, d6 0.093, d7 0.226, d8 0.423, d9 0.384. It is close to zero before trial 50, peaks in trials 80-89 and dips slightly after 90. The rise is convex rather than linear from 50, but that is a small point.

The belief claim is confirmed and is monotonic. Splitting the conjunction x ramp by belief bin (<0.2 ... >=0.8) gives weights 0.0122, 0.0111, 0.0090, 0.0039, 0.0009 (test 0.507). With a ramp x (1-belief) term, the plain ramp weight drops to about 0, so activation is roughly ramp times P(S2 good). One refinement: adding (belief_lo < -2) gets a negative weight and lifts test from 0.525 to 0.540, so the effect saturates or falls back slightly when the observer is very sure S2 is good.

The 'larger after a rare a2->S1 trial (+0.12)' claim depends on which other terms are in the fit. On its own, ramp x (prev_state==1) is positive (+0.45 relative to the base ramp weight of 0.78). Once (1-belief) is in the model, it turns negative (-0.33). An unrewarded rare S1 visit lowers belief, so the raw 'rare a2 trial' bump is mostly carried by belief. The +0.12 in the recorded fit is a flat late-episode bump next to the belief term, not a robust independent effect.

'After a rewarded a2 trial late in the episode it falls slightly below baseline (-0.05)' is a baseline artifact. The same -0.04 applies to every non-conjunction D2 cell, because the activation there is simply 0. It is not specific to rewarded a2 trials.

Misses show no large systematic error by phase or previous-trial pattern: phase mean errors are within +/-0.007 and the worst pattern errors are about 0.02, which is baseline leakage into the zero D2 cells. The remaining misses are the isolated 1.9-2.0 spikes, predicted at 0.5-0.6. Things I tried that do not explain them: two or three consecutive unrewarded a2 trials (+0.0006), belief_cover, trial-2 state or reward, trial-3 reward. They stay unexplained, as the original write-up said.

The cost of dropping the model's value and policy outputs could not be measured in this observed-only run (the tool rejects those terms). The firing scorecard's low-value cue appears to be largely covered by the ideal-observer belief.
